purpose: Determine whether observed or candidate market/lending-rate measures can be mapped directly into the observed ECB BSI private-credit transaction flow without conflating loan prices, new-business agreement volumes, realized net financial transactions, borrower demand and bank supply conditions.

ecb_mir.finding: MIR measures interest rates individually agreed between banks and customers and separately reports new-business volumes. New business includes newly agreed contracts and renegotiations, while MIR new-business rates reflect contemporaneous demand and supply conditions.
ecb_mir.implication: A lending rate is a price variable, not a realized credit-flow quantity. MIR new-business volume is also not definitionally the same object as BSI net financial transactions.

ecb_bsi.finding: BSI financial transactions are derived from changes in stocks after removing non-transaction effects such as reclassifications, revaluations, exchange-rate changes and loan write-offs/write-downs.
ecb_bsi.implication: The RMD credit_flow reference is a net transaction concept distinct from MIR rate observations and MIR agreement volumes.

ecb_bls.finding: BLS explicitly separates loan supply conditions/credit standards from loan demand; both help explain observed loan growth.
ecb_bls.implication: Observed credit transactions cannot identify a lending-rate-to-flow response without a design that separately controls or identifies supply and demand.

retained_rmd.finding: RMD already requires sector-specific supply/demand separation and does not admit the aggregate bank-credit response equation for calibration.

structural_interpretation.market_and_lending_rates_role: Price-side monetary/financial conditions. The generic node remains unresolved because household, NFC, market and outstanding-rate concepts are not one scalar.
structural_interpretation.credit_flow_role: Observed realized ECB BSI financial transaction for the frozen private non-financial credit boundary.
structural_interpretation.identification_requirement: Any quantitative rate-to-credit-flow relation must be preregistered on a sector-specific boundary with matched rate, credit-flow target, activity and separate supply/demand evidence. Predictive association does not establish a causal demand elasticity or supply response.
